title: Zipfian ingress topology sensitivity scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick exploration of how different front-end ingress topologies and skewed (Zipfian) arrival distributions interact with KV cache priming and cross-shard fan-in. Goal: find topology knobs that hurt p99 under realistic skew and write quick mitigation hypotheses.

Environment:
- Model: open-llm-small-v2 quantized int8 (prod-like weight shape)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v0.38.2 (local dev cluster w/ 4xA100 emulated nodes)
- Client: synthetic generator (zipfian alpha sweep) + real traffic replay sample (customer A, anonymized)
- Config knobs: ingress strategy {single-edge, per-region, shard-aware}, shard-count {4,8}, KV cache enabled true/false, batch max-token 1024, batching timeout 5ms, prefetch_enabled false
- Measurement: 1 minute warmup, 10 minute steady run, capture p50/p95/p99 latency, token/s throughput, KV hit rate, queue length histogram every 30s

Experiment plan (short):
1) Baseline: single-edge ingress, shard-count=4, KV on (cold start primed with 10% popular prefixes). Zipf alpha=1.1, QPS target=1200.
2) Increase skew: alpha=1.6, same baseline infra.
3) Topology variants for alpha=1.6: per-region edge (traffic split by locality), shard-aware routing (route popular prefixes to hot shard), and single-edge with backlog smoothing.
4) Shard scaling: run shard-count=8 with shard-aware routing.
5) Disable KV to verify effect.

Quick run notes (raw):
- Baseline (alpha=1.1): p50=24ms, p95=78ms, p99=210ms, throughput=1188 tok/s, kv_hit=0.62, mean queue_len=1.3
- High skew (alpha=1.6) single-edge: p50=26ms, p95=120ms, p99=520ms (spikes), throughput=1160, kv_hit=0.81, queue_len mean=3.7, observed 3 sustained 500ms+ outliers at minutes 4-6 corresponding to microbursts where hot-key dominated requests queued up at a single shard.
- High skew per-region: p50=28ms, p95=110ms, p99=360ms, throughput=1150, kv_hit per-region=0.79 overall. Slight improvement vs single-edge p99 but still elevated.
- High skew shard-aware routing: p50=25ms, p95=85ms, p99=140ms, throughput=1175, kv_hit=0.86, queue_len mean=1.6. Big win — moving hot prefixes to a targeted hot shard reduced cross-shard queueing and tail latency.
- Shard-count=8 + shard-aware: p50=24ms, p95=80ms, p99=120ms, throughput=1180, kv_hit=0.88. Diminishing returns vs 4 shards but slightly lower p99.
- KV disabled (alpha=1.6): p50=30ms, p95=160ms, p99=720ms, throughput decreased slightly to 1110, confirming KV cache is a major tail mitigation under skew.

ASCII chart (p99 across topologies, high-skew alpha=1.6):
- single-edge  | ######################### 520ms
- per-region   | ################### 360ms
- shard-aware  | ####### 140ms
- shard8 aware | ##### 120ms
- kv-off       | ######################################## 720ms

Observations / quick hypotheses:
- Zipfian skew amplifies cross-shard contention when ingress is naive; a single-edge that fans into shards without hot-key awareness concentrates hot-key load on shards, increasing queue length and p99.
- KV cache priming materially reduces tail for high-skew workloads. Higher kv_hit correlated with reduced p99 in these runs.
- Shard-aware routing (hot-key pinning) + modest shard count is an effective mitigation — it localizes hot-key load and preserves batching efficiency.
- Per-region helps when traffic has geographical locality but is brittle if hot keys cross regions or if hot-key concentration exceeds local shard capacity.
- Increasing shards helps but returns diminish; better to combine routing + KV priming than infinite sharding.

Notes-to-self / follow-ups:
- Re-run with prefetch_enabled=true and a 50% priming coverage to quantify prefetch cost vs tail benefit (TODO: PERF ticket).
- Compare against real customer A replay with timestamps to ensure microburst shapes align with synthetic zipfian.
- Add instrumentation to track "hot-key handoff" events where ingress reassigns a prefix to another shard; measure handoff latency and effect on p99.
- Talk to Marta about embedding shard-aware routing prototype into ingress gate (possible hot-key registry).
- Small action item: add a circuit-breaker threshold for queue_len>5 on a shard to trigger temporary routing fallback (A/B test).

Open questions / constraints:
- How stable are hot keys over long windows? If hotness churns quickly, pinning may cause thrash. Need churn study.
- Cost: extra metadata for shard-aware routing plus coordination might add 3-5% overhead; need to measure CPU impact.
- Safety: ensure routing changes are gradual (canary) to avoid global cascades.

Bottom line (one-liner): For Zipfian-skew workloads, combine KV priming + shard-aware hot-key routing before simply increasing shard count — gives large p99 reduction at lower cost.

Version notes and scratch history:
- 2024-10-22: initial runs, baseline + high-skew single-edge
- 2024-10-25: added shard-aware prototype and shard=8 runs (Marta helped instrument)
- 2024-11-05: added KV-off validation and compiled notes
